title: Hammocks for a free factor agree with ordinary inversion
statement: Use simplicial categories and weak homotopy equivalences as in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. For an ordinary category $P$ with a wide subcategory $T$, write $H(P,T)(x,y)_k$ for reduced commutative rectangular zigzags with $k+1$ rows from $x$ to $y$: vertical arrows point down and lie in $T$, endpoint vertical arrows are identities, each horizontal column has uniform direction, leftward arrows lie in $T$, directions alternate, and no column is entirely identities. Include the length-zero diagram when $x=y$. Operators delete or repeat rows and then reduce by deleting identity columns and composing adjacent columns with the same direction. Composition concatenates and reduces. For a simplicial pair $(A,U)$ with a fixed object set, $\operatorname{diag}H(A,U)(x,y)_n=H(A_n,U_n)(x,y)_n$, with both simplicial operators applied together. Let $O$ be a small set and let $D,V$ be free ordinary categories with object set $O$: each has a chosen set of nonidentity generating arrows, and every arrow has a unique finite composable word in those generators, with the empty word representing an identity. Let $P=D*_O V$ be their coproduct among categories with object set $O$ and functors fixing $O$, and identify $V$ with its canonical wide subcategory of $P$. Let $P[V^{-1}]$ be the category with the same objects obtained by adjoining inverses to arrows of $V$, subject to the composition and inverse relations. Regard its mapping sets as discrete simplicial sets. Sending a hammock to the composite of any row in $P[V^{-1}]$, using inverses for leftward arrows, defines a simplicial functor $H(P,V)\to P[V^{-1}]$ which is the identity on objects and induces a weak homotopy equivalence on every mapping simplicial set. This functor is natural for functors of such pairs preserving $V$; no chosen generators need be preserved by these functors.
